evidence-grounded.why: The criterion holds for all three lines. Line 1 (PASS) names the wrong builds it tried: "uppercasing only the name (Hello, ADA!)", broken name parsing and a different flag name. It says the exact-output run of `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` catches each one. Its claim that bin/greet.js skips arguments starting with '--' is true: the code uses `find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'))`. Line 2 (PASS) names two wrong builds, uppercasing by default and changing greeting(). The run and the existing cli test in test/greet.test.js both catch them, and that test is real. Line 3 (FAIL) gives the concrete reason it can only be checked after merge: pages.yml publishes docs/ only on push to main. It also notes that the current docs/index.md has no --shout. Both facts are correct. Every file, script and behaviour cited exists in the repository.

catches-traps.why: The must_catch list has one item: line 3 has to FAIL because it can only be checked after merge, and the output has to point at pages.yml or the publish-on-push. The output gives line 3 "result": "FAIL" with the evidence "This can only be checked after merge. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes docs/ to Pages only on push to main". That names both pages.yml and the push-to-main trigger. It also suggests a fix that can be checked in the repo: docs/index.md documents --shout. The wrong_build section makes the same point again. The one item is fully covered, so the criterion is met.

avoids-must-not.why: The must_not list has one item: a FAIL on line 1 or line 2. I checked the result for each line in the output. Line 1 (--shout prints HELLO, ADA!) is "PASS". Line 2 (without --shout it still prints Hello, Ada!) is "PASS". Only line 3, the published docs page, is "FAIL". That FAIL and the overall "FAIL" result are not in the must_not list. So the output does nothing the must_not list forbids.
